messages:
Sara (PM): Quick sync request — can we run a 30m RICE workshop to lock the order for the Optimize toolkit (quantization / batching / caching)? Need launch criteria and rollout guardrails.
Diego (Eng): Wed 10am works for me. I can bring perf baselines and rough infra effort estimates.
Mina (Research): I can pull customer asks and eval diffs for quantization and caching. Wed is fine.
Alex (ML): Proposed agenda: 1) evidence + customer signals 2) impact definitions 3) effort & infra deps 4) RICE scoring and decision.
Jenna (Product): Also want acceptance criteria baked in: p95 latency target, token-cost delta threshold, and quality regression tolerance on evals.
Diego (Eng): Topline numbers from infra: batching can cut token cost ~15-25% for multi-turn; quantization reduces model memory ~35-45% but needs kernel work and validation; caching can reduce repeated-prefix token spend ~20-35% for chat-heavy apps.
Mina (Research): Note: several enterprise prospects flagged cache/privacy requirements — will need opt-in controls + audit logs for Private.
Tim (Ops): Ops note: Dedicated infra can allow larger batch windows if SLOs permit. We also need runtime feature flags for canary and safe fallback.
Sara (PM): Good — let's capture non-dev work (policy, compliance, docs).
Alex (ML): Draft RICE sketch (we should normalize Reach definitions):
```
Feature | Reach (users impacted) | Impact (1-10) | Confidence (%) | Effort (pts) -> RICE
Quantization | 50 | 8 | 65 | 5 -> R*I*C/E
Batching      | 45 | 6 | 80 | 2 -> ...
Caching       | 30 | 5 | 55 | 3 -> ...
```
Need standardized scales before scoring.
Diego (Eng): Can we define Reach as percent of token workload affected? Quant touches most model-serving calls, batching mainly affects multi-request and streaming patterns, caching affects conversational prefixes.
Mina (Research): Sales signal: quantization directly unlocks some on-prem deals because of GPU memory limits. Cache is a repeated ask from PLG customers but has compliance caveats.
Jenna (Product): Proposed launch criteria per feature: 
- Quantization: end-to-end eval regression <1.5% on canonical sets, automated quant-checks in CI, staged canary by model size.
- Batching: p95 latency increase <= 10ms for latency-sensitive routes, dashboarding + tracing.
- Caching: privacy opt-in controls, cache invalidation rules, audit logging and docs.
Sara (PM): My initial prioritization thought: 1) Quantization (high enterprise leverage), 2) Batching (fast wins for hosted cost), 3) Caching (product + policy work). But open to debate.
Diego (Eng): Counter: batching is low dev effort and can deliver immediate hosted cost savings; quant needs kernel/runtime work and thorough validation.
Mina (Research): Counter-counter: quant is blocker for several private deployments; sales timeline pushes it earlier.
Alex (ML): Suggest parallel tracks where possible: ship a lightweight batching path for hosted customers while core quant kernel work runs on its own track. Caching needs product decisions so likely slower.
Tim (Ops): Runtime dependency note: we should invest in feature-flag/canary hooks in the serving runtime first. That work unlocks safer rollout for batching and quant.
Jenna (Product): If we must sequence, I prefer quant -> batching -> caching given enterprise revenue impact. If we can parallelize, do batching for hosted and quant for private concurrently.
Sara (PM): Action items before Wed workshop: 
- Diego: firm infra effort, SLO constraints, and risks (due Tue COB).
- Mina: customer signal summary + eval diffs for quant/caching (due Tue COB).
- Alex: canonical RICE sheet with definitions and scoring rubric (due Tue COB).
- Jenna: formal acceptance criteria and risk table per feature (due Tue COB).
- Tim: runtime feature-flag checklist and canary rollout plan (due Tue COB).
Sara (PM): I'll create the invite for Wed 10am. Please react with :thumbsup: if you can make it.
